diagnosis: The scenario fails because the model defaults to cautious, standard legal practices that satisfy the checks without needing the hidden information. Specifically, C3 (linked to PF1) is satisfied by the model's default tendency to require commercial use consent, and C4/C5 (linked to PF2) are satisfied by the model's inherent bias toward prohibiting patient-level data and requiring de-identification in any clinical research context.

C4.why: The product and privacy confirmation changes the publication terms from the draft's unrestricted permission to a prohibition on patient-level data and mandatory de-identification before any permitted external publication.
